newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds were weaker on the day but above their session lows by the close.

Traders said the Swiss bond futures contract, or "Conf," came under early pressure when the market opened. Its declines were seen partly linked to selling after Germany's Bund lost ground on Wednesday after the Conf had already closed.
The June Conf hit a contract low of 117.50 during the session but ended at 117.60, down 45 basis points.
The Bund was down nine basis points at 99.69.
Swiss-based traders were watching key support levels for both contracts.
One traders said 99.40/45 would be support for the Bund, with major support seen at 99.25/28.

The June Conf was supported by the time it dipped to 117.50, where one trader said only a few contracts changed hands. "I think that we are levels where it cannot fall much more. Shorts are being covered," he said.
Overall market volume was high in both directions.

The 4-1/2 percent June 2007 cash bond was seen supported around the closing level of 106.00. The price dipped to 105.80, but volume was scant. The market is waiting to see if the 2007 will be reopened at next week's Swiss Treasury auction.
While the 2007 cash bond fell by roughly a point, shorter rates were steady, leading traders to expect that the trend towards curve steepening would continue.
